title: Chicken Piccata
subtitle: Pan-fried chicken in a lemon, caper, and butter sauce
excerpt: Thin chicken escalopes cooked in a white wine, lemon, and caper sauce finished with cold butter. An Italian-American staple adapted from the original veal piccata, quick to cook and sharp with citrus.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chicken piccata is an Italian-American dish adapted from veal piccata, the traditional Italian version. The word piccata refers to the sharp, acidic flavour profile, pungent, from the Italian piccante. Veal piccata originated in northern Italy; the chicken version was popularised in the United States during the twentieth century when veal became more expensive and chicken escalopes were substituted. The capers are an Italian-American addition not found in the original.

content.text: Chicken piccata depends on thin escalopes, if the chicken breast is thick, butterfly it and then beat it between cling film with a rolling pin to about 1 cm. The sauce is made in the same pan immediately after the chicken is cooked, so the fond from the browning becomes part of it. The butter goes in cold, cut into cubes, swirled off the heat to emulsify into the sauce. Do not let it boil after the butter is added.

items.preparation: juice of both, zest of one

content.text: Season the chicken and dust in flour, shaking off the excess. Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through. Remove to a plate and keep warm.
Pour the wine into the hot pan and deglaze, scraping up the browned bits. Let it reduce by half. Add the stock and lemon juice and simmer for 2 minutes.
Remove the pan from the heat. Add the cold butter cubes a few at a time, swirling the pan constantly until the sauce is glossy and emulsified. Add the capers and lemon zest. Taste for salt.
Return the chicken to the pan for 1 minute to warm through. Scatter with parsley and serve immediately with pasta or sautéed potatoes.
